taxonomyNote: NatureServe and Animal Diversity Web use the name Upland Chorus Frog for Pseudacris feriarum (NatureServe lists synonym Pseudacris triseriata feriarum); 'southeastern chorus frog' is the batch's name.
fieldMarks: Small; females 25-33 mm, males 23-31 mm; brown, tan or gray.
Three stripes (sometimes broken into spots) down the back, often a dark triangle between the eyes (absent in some South Carolina populations).
Belly light tan to white; breeding males have brownish-yellow throats; calls a trill.
behavior: Breeds in temporary pools, not permanent water; choruses can be heard by day and night in the breeding season.
Does not wander more than about 200 m from breeding sites after breeding and is found in leaf litter; southern populations may stay active all year.
Insectivore eating ants, beetles, flies, caterpillars, springtails, mites and snails; sit-and-wait feeder.
habitat: Meadows, moist forests, bottomland swamps and areas near ponds and bogs; mainly upland in the north and lowland in the south; uses ditches, flooded pastures and rain pools.
range: Southeastern United States: southeastern Missouri, northeastern Arkansas and eastern Mississippi east to coastal Virginia and the Carolinas, north to central and southern Pennsylvania, south to northern Florida. Not in Canada.
